world.title: Somalia Security Ties Revive as Police Officers Graduate with Master's Degrees After Four Decades
world.description: MOSCOW – Four senior officers of the Somali Police Force have graduated with Master’s degrees from Russia’s Academy of Management under the Ministry of Internal Affairs, marking the first such graduation in four decades and signaling a revival of bilateral security cooperation between Mogadishu and Moscow. The officers, who specialised in General Administration and Strategic Planning, received their qualifications at a ceremony held at the Academy of Administration in Russia. Somali police authorities described the achievement as one that would strengthen leadership and institutional capacity within the force, with the officers expected to apply their expertise in strategic planning, public administration and institutional management as Somalia continues reforms aimed at modernising its security sector. A Historic Milestone After Four Decades The graduation represents a significant milestone, marking the first time in more than 40 years that Somali police officers have completed advanced studies at a Russian institution. Government officials hailed the event as a revival of educational and security cooperation between Somalia and Russia, which had largely lain dormant since the collapse of the Siad Barre regime in 1991. During the Cold War, Somalia and the Soviet Union maintained close military and security ties, with hundreds of Somali officers receiving training in Russian institutions. That relationship collapsed after Somalia’s civil war, but the graduation of the four officers suggests a renewed interest on both sides in rebuilding security-sector ties. A Diversifying Security Partnership Landscape The graduation comes as Somalia pursues a diversified foreign policy, expanding international partnerships for security training with countries including Turkey, Egypt, Italy, Uganda, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. Russia, for its part, has been seeking to deepen its diplomatic and security engagement across Africa, with Moscow continuing to provide assistance to Somalia in the form of police training. science.title: Quality and reliability of videos about pneumoconiosis on TikTok and Bilibili in China
science.description: Pneumoconiosis is a common occupational lung disease, and social media platforms such as TikTok and Bilibili have become important sources of health information. However, the quality and reliability of video content on these platforms remain unclear. In this cross-sectional study, 163 pneumoconiosis-related videos from TikTok and Bilibili in China were included. Information on video characteristics, uploader types, content themes, and presentation formats was extracted. We assessed video quality and reliability using GQS, mDISCERN, JAMA benchmark criteria, and VIQI. Correlation analysis was further performed to examine associations between video metrics and quality scores. TikTok videos had shorter durations and lower GQS (P = 0.002) and mDISCERN (P = 0.041) scores than Bilibili videos. In the combined analysis, mDISCERN and JAMA scores varied significantly across uploader groups. On TikTok, GQS, mDISCERN, and JAMA scores differed by uploader type, whereas on Bilibili, differences were observed for mDISCERN and JAMA scores. Correlation analysis further indicated that longer videos were negatively correlated with mDISCERN and JAMA scores on TikTok, but positively correlated with GQS scores on Bilibili. Pneumoconiosis-related videos on TikTok and Bilibili showed limited quality and reliability. Greater involvement from medical practitioners and stronger platform-specific regulatory strategies are needed to improve the educational value of health information on both platforms.
